paper.title: Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Domain-Specific Calibration Dynamics in Prediction Markets
paper.method: Cell-level logistic recalibration logit P(y=1)=a+b*logit(p) on trades (domain x time-to-resolution x trade size), variance decomposition, market/event-clustered bootstrap, Bayesian measurement-error model
missing_info: Polymarket trade-level snapshot (2.17 GB parquet) is not deposited in the code repo; only its SHA-256
Exact Polymarket bin-level slopes are in supplementary/calibration_matrix_216.csv (not re-derived here)
paper.verified_by: Claude, 2026-10-20: arXiv abstract page, repo README, DATA_SNAPSHOT_NOTE.md, src/config.py, src/calibration.py, src/classify.py

claims.statement: Polymarket political markets are underconfident: the logistic recalibration slope exceeds 1 (prices compressed toward 50%).
claims.dataset: Polymarket unified snapshot, Politics domain, reliable time bins (0-1h and 1-3h excluded)

reported.source: repo DATA_SNAPSHOT_NOTE.md, 'Politics mean slope (reliable bins)', revised snapshot

claims.notes: Reported value is a mean over trade-level cells; our market-level single-horizon estimate is not numerically comparable, only the direction (>1) is tested.

claims.statement: On Polymarket, the large-trade ('whale') effect on political calibration is not significant under market-clustered bootstrap.
claims.notes: Needs trade-level data with sizes; not testable with the market-level design. Status stays NOT_STARTED.

assumptions.chosen: One YES price per market at a fixed horizon before the reference time, unweighted
assumptions.rationale: Trade-level history (paper's unit) is a 36 GB dump; market-level prices are public via prices-history. Tests the direction of the claim, not its magnitude.
The outcome can become known between scheduled end and close; using the later time would leak the result into the price.

assumptions.chosen: Newton-Raphson MLE with L2 on slope only, C=10, prices clipped to [0.01, 0.99]
assumptions.rationale: Same objective and clipping as the paper's sklearn fit_logistic.

assumptions.chosen: Paper's Polymarket regex, verbatim, first match (Sports > Politics > Crypto > Finance)
30 hours before the reference time (paper bin 24-48h, a reliable bin)
assumptions.rationale: Avoids the unreliable 0-1h/1-3h bins; secondary horizons are descriptive only.

assumptions.chosen: YES token only, outcome 1 if YES resolved true
assumptions.rationale: Logistic recalibration is symmetric; using both sides would double-count each market.
Strictly after the paper's data cut-off: the paper never saw these markets.

assumptions.chosen: Only umaResolutionStatus=resolved with outcomePrices exactly [1,0] or [0,1]; horizon price must be within 6h before the target
assumptions.rationale: Disputed, voided or partial resolutions and stale prices are excluded and counted, never back-filled.
Markets in one event are dependent (paper also reports event-clustered results).

decision_rule.INSUFFICIENT_DATA: fewer than 100 markets or fewer than 30 events, or no valid interval
decision_rule.REVIEW_REQUIRED: market listing did not reach the last page in every month, the market cap was reached, or more than 2% of horizon-price fetches failed; never reported as PASS/FAIL

preregistration.not_a_trade_signal: A calibration finding is not an after-cost trading edge and is never promoted automatically.

amendments.change: Added REVIEW_REQUIRED for a truncated market listing (stricter, not looser).

Disclosure: experiment code sat under an 'experiments/' path ignored by the repository .gitignore, so it was NOT included in commits b614813/c56aff8; only this ledger (incl. the decision rule) was. Code moved to studies/ and committed after the full run had started; the SHA-256 of the exact files used by the run is recorded here.

After run-1 (listing truncated at 4000 pages, months Jul-Sep under-represented; status REVIEW_REQUIRED, kept as-is): listing split into calendar months, each must reach its last page; reaching --max-markets is also REVIEW_REQUIRED. Decision thresholds unchanged.

After run-2 aborted on one network failure (no result produced): a failed price fetch excludes that market (counted as HISTORY_FETCH_FAILED); more than 2% failures, or a failed month listing, is REVIEW_REQUIRED. Decision thresholds unchanged.
